_comment: D-SINK-16. The one rule that decides whether an ADOPTED mpv process is safe
to hand a credentialed URL and the provider headers to, written once and run
by both implementations: Model.tlsPropertiesSafe (tests/Model.test.js) and
tls_properties_safe in the helper, bin/helper/08-player-verbs.py (tests/test_mpv.py).
`verify` is mpv's `tls-verify` property as its JSON IPC answers it, and
`optionCount` is how many entries `stream-lavf-o` holds -- a COUNT and never
the keys or the values, because that map can carry a proxy address with
credentials in it and the number crosses into the shell (engineering rule 5).
FFmpeg's own `tls_verify` AVOption outvotes mpv's option (measured,
D-SINK-13 layer 3), so a non-empty map is unsafe whatever is in it.
The vectors deliberately include the shapes a double would be tempted to
accept -- 1, "yes", false-as-zero -- because mpv answers a flag with a JSON
boolean and nothing else, and a reader more forgiving than the thing it reads
is how this exposure survives its own fix.
One shape is deliberately NOT a vector: a count of 0.0. Python's reader
distinguishes 0.0 from 0 and JavaScript's cannot, so the two mirrors would
disagree on it. It cannot arise -- the count is len() on a map in the helper
and the integer that JSON carries in the shell -- and a vector the two
languages must answer differently would be a vector that teaches the wrong
lesson. Model.playerTls refuses a fractional count outright for the same
reason.
2026-10-29 (D-SINK-43/44): a third reading, `unpinned`, the number of OTHER TLS
pins the player does not hold, summed by the helper (read_tls_state): the TLS
entries of `demuxer-lavf-o` -- for HLS and DASH libavformat hands that map to
every segment open, so `tls_verify=0` or `verifyhost=<the attacker's name>`
there undoes verification with both --tls-verify=yes tokens in place (measured)
-- plus 1 when `load-auto-profiles` is not off, plus every [protocol.*] or
[extension.*] profile that could set, at file load and so after this read, an
option this player does not have set from the command line. Zero is the only
safe count, for the same reasons as optionCount, and the same shapes are
refused: null, a boolean, a negative, a fraction, a string.
The two mpv property names, which both languages spell as their own
literal. Nothing joins two literals but a name, so the name is pinned
here and asserted against each side's constant (CLAUDE.md rule 13): a
rename on one side only would make every read answer `property not
found`, which the verdict reads as `stop` - every adopted player in the
field stopped on reattach.
